1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6.background: Named after the Belgian grandmaster Albéric O'Kelly de Galway, who won the Belgian championship thirteen times between 1937 and 1959.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3.strategy: The main answer: White prepares d4 and a broad pawn centre, as in the usual c3 set-up against the Sicilian, but with the knight already developed for free because ...a6 does little against this plan. Black has to meet the coming centre at once.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Venice System

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c4.strategy: Uses the spare tempo to clamp down on the centre before the knight reaches c3: the pawns on c4 and e4 together control d5, and c4 also takes b5 away, so Black's ...b5 plan is stopped. A slow, strategic game in which White enjoys more space.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c4.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Maróczy Bind

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4.strategy: Opens the centre at once, as in any open game. It is sound, but here ...a6 is a useful extra move for Black: the knight can no longer jump to b5, and Black can strike back in the centre with ...e5 and equalise comfortably.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Normal System

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.Nc3.strategy: Guards e4 and keeps the open game in hand: White can still play d4 next and reach familiar open positions, with ...a6 not necessarily wasted for Black. A flexible, low-risk choice that does not try to punish the move order.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.Nc3.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Yerevan System

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.Be2.strategy: A modest developing move that prepares castling and keeps the bishop out of reach of ...b5. It neither fights for the centre nor exploits the slow ...a6, so Black is free to expand on the queenside.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.Be2.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Aronin System

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.b3.strategy: Prepares to fianchetto the queen's bishop on the long diagonal, aiming at the centre and the kingside. Solid but slow: White gives Black time to take space in the centre.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.b3.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Kieseritzky System

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d3.strategy: A quiet set-up that supports e4 and leaves the other pieces free to choose their squares. It avoids theory, but it gives up the fight for the centre and offers Black an easy game.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d3.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Quiet System

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.g3.strategy: Prepares to fianchetto the king's bishop, where it supports e4 and pressures the long diagonal. Sound and flexible, but White spends time on the flank and does not challenge Black's centre.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.g3.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Réti System

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.b4.strategy: A wing gambit that tries to deflect the c-pawn, which guards d4. After 3...cxb4 Black is simply a pawn up and White has no concrete lead in development to show for it.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.b4.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Wing Gambit

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 d5.strategy: The natural central reply: Black challenges e4 at once and denies White the broad pawn centre. White's c3 pawn takes away the c3 square, so a queen recapture on d5 cannot be hit by a knight there.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 Nf6.strategy: Attacks e4 at once and forces White to decide whether to advance or defend it. If the pawn advances, Black's knight lands on a central square and Black fights White's space gain by pressure on the pawn chain.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 Nf6.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Venice System, Barcza Line

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 b5.strategy: Uses the a6 move: Black gains queenside space and prepares a bishop on the long diagonal against e4. The cost is a loosened queenside, where White can aim at the advanced pawns.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 b5.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Venice System, Ljubojevic Line

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 d6.strategy: Concedes the centre to White: the solid pawn on d6 blocks Black's own bishop and does not challenge e4. Black plans a compact fianchetto set-up, but White gets space and the easier game.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 d6.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Venice System, Steiner Line

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c4 e6.strategy: The usual master choice: Black frees the dark-squared bishop and covers d5 and f5, accepting less space. A compact set-up, from which Black waits for White to commit in the centre.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c4 e6.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Maróczy Bind, Paulsen Line

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c4 d6.strategy: A sturdy pawn on d6 holds e5 and prepares a kingside fianchetto, so the bishop works against the d4 square. A playable way to meet the clamp, though the d6 pawn can become a target.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c4 d6.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Maróczy Bind, Robatsch Line

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4.strategy: The standard capture: Black trades a wing pawn for White's central one, opens the c-file and ends up with a central pawn majority. The a-pawn has already taken b5 away from White's knight.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 d5 4.exd5.strategy: Takes the pawn at once and makes Black justify the central break. Black must recapture or compensate for the pawn, while White aims for a broad pawn centre and keeps a small, lasting edge.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 d5 4.exd5 Nf6.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Venice System, Gambit Line
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.c3 d5 4.exd5 Nf6.strategy: Develops with an attack on d5 instead of recapturing, a pawn offer for quick development and pressure on White's pawns. White can hold the extra pawn, and it is doubtful that Black's play fully pays for it.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4.strategy: Recaptures with a centralised knight and heads into open play. Here ...a6 stops the knight from jumping to b5, so White has to find other squares for it and Black has gained a useful move.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4 4.c3.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Normal System, Smith-Morra Line
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4 4.c3.strategy: A pawn sacrifice for quick development and open lines: if Black takes, White recaptures with a piece and gets a lead in development with pressure on the c- and d-files. Playable, but Black stands a pawn up if it defends accurately.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Qxd4.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Normal System, Zagorovsky Line
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Qxd4.strategy: Brings the queen to the centre at once, but ...Nc6 attacks it with a gain of tempo for Black. A slightly eccentric way to recapture that costs time, though the position stays playable.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Bc4.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Normal System, Cortlever Gambit
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Bc4.strategy: Leaves the d4 pawn alone and develops the bishop toward f7, but White is a pawn down and ...b5 gains time against the bishop. White has no more than the plain recapture offers, and the pawn remains a problem.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 e5.name: Sicilian Defence: O'Kelly Variation, Normal System, Taimanov Line
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 a6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 e5.strategy: Challenges the knight at once, using ...a6 which takes b5 away, so the knight must retreat to a less useful square. Black gains central space but leaves the d5 square without a pawn guard.
